html:
Mswati III has been king of Swaziland since 1986, when he was crowned at 18, and is the last absolute monarch in Africa.

The son of Sobhuza II, he studied in England before taking the throne. He rules with wide powers: he appoints the prime minister and many members of parliament, and political parties cannot run in elections. A constitution in 2005 kept most of his powers.

He has many wives and his family's spending has been criticised in a country with high poverty and the world's highest HIV rate. In 2018 he renamed the country Eswatini, its name in the Swazi language. Pro-democracy protests were crushed in 2021.
